Input images: Image 1 is the canonical facade and must be followed exactly. Image 2 is an alignment study that identifies the fixed transom error; use it only to understand what must be preserved.
Primary request: Show the existing centered double doors opened inward by about 20 degrees.
Critical geometry: The doorway has an arched blue-gray canopy and a separate fixed horizontal transom panel above the moving leaves. Preserve that upper fixed panel and its strong horizontal crossbar exactly as part of the doorway frame. The transom is the rectangular strip immediately above the leaves (in canonical 640x360 coordinates about x306..334, y214..226). The two moving leaves begin below it, about y227, and extend only to y264. Rotate only these lower leaves inward; never extend leaves into the fixed transom, never replace or erase the transom.
Keep the exact canonical camera and facade: doorway center x320, red side columns, roof, brick, windows, trees, sidewalk and street all match Image 1 in position and appearance. Black uniform gap only between the slightly open lower leaves, interior dark. Crisp original pixel art. No new architecture, steps, objects, people, text, UI, framing change, zoom or crop. Output one horizontal 16:9 frame.

Maintain the arched blue-gray canopy, red side columns, exact doorway proportions and center position. Black unlit empty interior.
Preserve Image 1's original facade geometry, pixel-art palette and wide camera framing. No architecture changes, no new steps, objects, text, UI, people, crop, zoom or reframing.
